title: Cross Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
definition: CSRF forces a logged-in user's browser to send a forged HTTP request, including their session cookies, to a vulnerable web application, executing an unwanted action (like transferring money).
simpleExplanation: You are logged into your bank. You click a funny picture on a hacker's website, but hidden in the code is a request that tells your bank to wire money. Because you are logged in, your browser automatically attaches your cookie, and the bank approves the transfer.
diagramContent: sequenceDiagram participant User participant EvilSite as Evil.com participant Bank Note over User,Bank: User is logged into Bank (has Cookie) User->>EvilSite: Visits site EvilSite-->>User: Returns HTML with hidden Note over User: Browser automatically attempts to load image User->>Bank: GET /transfer?amt=500 (Browser auto-attaches Cookie!) Note over Bank: Validates cookie, transfers money

answers.question: What is the main tradeoff of CSRF?
answers.answer: Usually a tradeoff between Server CPU usage, TTFB (Time to First Byte), and Client CPU usage.
